chunks: Ahmad ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Safwan, from Khalid ibn Najih, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Convey the greeting of peace to those of your companions whom you meet, and say to them that so-and-so, son of so-and-so, sends you greetings of peace.

And say to them: Adhere to taqwa (God-consciousness) of God — Mighty and Majestic — and what can be attained through it of what is with God. I swear by God, I do not command you except with what we command our own selves.

So adhere to diligence and striving. And when you have performed the morning prayer and dispersed, rise early in seeking your livelihood, and seek the permissible, for God — Mighty and Majestic — will sustain you and assist you in it.

key_terms.الجد والاجتهاد: Diligence and striving — practical effort and earnest application in one's worldly and religious affairs
key_terms.الحلال: The permissible (halal) — lawfully earned livelihood, contrasted with forbidden (haram) means
key_terms.السلام: The Islamic greeting of peace — also a divine attribute; spreading it strengthens community bonds
key_terms.تقوى الله: God-consciousness (taqwa) — the foundational ethical disposition of fear and awareness of God, the foundation of righteous action

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about earning a livelihood and spreading greetings?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses his followers through an intermediary, instructing them to spread the greeting of peace among one another, maintain taqwa, and pursue lawful livelihood through diligent effort after the morning prayer. This hadith reflects the Imam's practice of sending moral instruction through trusted companions during periods when direct public teaching was restricted under Abbasid rule. The injunction to 'rise early after Fajr prayer' aligns with the Islamic ethic that worship and worldly endeavor are complementary, not opposed.
